pairs.difference: A: floating jacket in a three-quarter view. The collar opening is seen from above and both cuffs show their holes, but the hem stays a flat band. B: hat with an upright crown, the left brim showing its top and the right brim showing its underside, which a curled brim can explain. Each card has one small view question and neither is clearly worse. Planar shares of 0.116 and 0.426 are both in range.

A: neck pillow tilted in space, with a smooth rainbow that suits a truly inflated form and one consistent view. B: flat photo card almost square to the camera, with no visible convergence and a blank normal map. Its planar share of 1.0 is above the real range, but that comes from the flat subject and says little about the camera. A flat card gives no evidence of the view.

A: wristband as a tilted ring, turned three-quarter. The near face is wide, the far rim is thin, and the icons wrap with the curve in one view, like the real telescope's turned pose. B: star badge almost face-on with no turn, showing only a thin side edge at lower right, and the pin sits out at the side. It reads as flat relief on a patterned backdrop with little depth. Evidence is weak because the real podium and fan are also frontal.
pairs.fix: Turn the star badge about 30 degrees and tip it back so one side recedes. Show the thick metal edge along the near side and let the pin pass behind the badge.

pairs.difference: A: high camera looking down on the dock. The tops of both posts, the planks and the water all share one downward angle. B: the distant mesas put the horizon near the lower storey, and the cornices are seen from below. The porch roof above that horizon still shows a broad top face, reading green like the ground, so the upper and lower parts lean toward different camera heights. The sloped roof could partly explain this, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Set one camera at chest height. Show the porch roof narrow and steeply foreshortened, with only a thin sliver of its top, and keep the horizon behind the porch.

pairs.difference: A: saddle in near-pure side view on a rail that runs straight across the card, with no recession. There is no ground plane, yet a soft contact shadow sits under the stirrup, and the stirrup tread shows its top face. The saddle therefore hangs in air and sits on a floor at once. B: ball on sand seen from above, with sand rising behind it and a shadow that seats it firmly. It has one clear view.
pairs.fix: Turn the saddle three-quarter so the rail recedes into the card with mild convergence. Remove the shadow under the stirrup and let it hang free.

pairs.difference: A: tray from a raised three-quarter camera, with the table planks, tray top and cube tops all at one angle. The near corner is enlarged, but the object stays in one view, like the real camera card. B: pot in near-side view with a very shallow base ellipse. The logs below splay out at a more downward angle, and the pot base floats above them with no contact, so the top and bottom of the object do not sit on one ground plane.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera over the logs so they match the pot's low view. Rest the pot base directly on the logs with visible contact, and keep the sand at one flat angle.

pairs.difference: A: the coil is seen clearly from above, while the loop hangs in air as a tilted hoop with its own plane. The wooden beam recedes at a third angle, so the three parts do not agree on one floor. Planar share of 0.001 is below the real range, though the thin rope accounts for part of that. B: both shoes share one raised three-quarter view on a level floor with a straight wall line, and each casts a shadow that matches.
pairs.fix: Lay the loop and the coil on the same tilt, seen from the same slightly raised camera, and make the beam top match that angle.

pairs.difference: A: dead-frontal camera with the pot on the centre axis and arms mirrored in flat profile. The ledge is a level band with no recession, and the swollen arms show smooth rainbow normals. Planar share of 0.014 is below the real range, with only the rim ellipse saying the camera is above. B: vending machine turned three-quarter, with a narrow side face, flat even front patches, a thin top face and feet on a soft floor line, all in one mild perspective.
pairs.fix: Turn the scene slightly so the pot and the ledge corner show a receding side. Draw the cactus ribs as distinct faces rather than an inflated balloon surface.

pairs.difference: A: the shaft mouth is seen from above and shows the inside back wall, while the raised toe also shows the underside of the sole. The boot's top and bottom both face the viewer, so the top and foot do not share one view. B: cap board is an even planar patch seen from above, and the lower band curves the same way. It has one clear view and mild perspective.
pairs.fix: Show the boot in one view from slightly above. Keep the sole hidden except for its thin edge and show only a shallow ellipse at the boot opening.

pairs.difference: A: bottle lying in sand at one consistent angle, with foreground sand, the hero, and simpler dark rocks and weed behind, matching the real layered scenes. B: stacked map sheets lying flat at one tilt with folded lower edges. Its planar share of 0.741 is above the range because the subject is flat paper. The fanned sheets agree with each other, so nothing here separates the two on viewpoint.

A: low street-level camera with strong convergence toward the rear, which is forced but consistent. The roof, windows and road all run to one side. B: the desert horizon sits at mid-boiler height, yet the funnel high above it shows its open top ellipse from above. The track and cowcatcher are also seen from well above, while the near end swells wide-angle. The funnel and the horizon disagree on camera height.
pairs.fix: Set the camera at wheel-top height. Show the funnel rim from slightly below with no inside visible, and reduce the swelling of the front so the cab and cowcatcher are closer in scale.

pairs.difference: A: the arched canvas opening faces the viewer almost head-on, yet the wheels on the side, perpendicular to it, are also nearly round. Two faces at right angles cannot both be that frontal, so the front and side of the wagon use different views. The hard floor line also stays level with no recession. B: the fountain's basin, tiers and paving rings all narrow steadily toward eye level, a single consistent high view.
pairs.fix: Use one three-quarter view: draw the wheels as clear narrow ellipses and the front opening as a foreshortened arch turned away, with the side of the wagon bed receding.

pattern: What still gives generated cards away is disagreement between parts of the object rather than wide-angle lens alone: the top and bottom of a form are seen from different camera heights, perpendicular faces are both frontal (wagon, boot, funnel against horizon), and contact with the ground is weak or contradictory (stirrup shadow, floating pot). The lessons run the same way: generated cards have a higher camera, a looming near end, swollen rainbow forms and a curved ground plane, while real cards keep crisp flat patches, mild perspective and one view. Flat subjects give no reading: planar_share of 1.0 or 0.741 comes from the paper, not the camera.
